records.organization_name: City of Alexandria Office of the Commonwealth's Attorney
records.location_name: Victim-Witness Assistance Program (VWAP) & VSTOP – Office of the Commonwealth's Attorney
records.notes: Public prosecutor's office (not a shelter). VWAP and VSTOP advocates provide court accompaniment, safety planning, crisis intervention, referrals, restitution help and Virginia Victims Fund applications; dedicated Domestic Violence Intervention Specialist for survivors of domestic abuse, intimate partner violence or sexual assault. VWAP/VSTOP are NOT bound by the same confidentiality standards as other victim support services (systems-based prosecution office). 24/7 hotlines: Domestic Violence 703.746.4911; Sexual Assault 703.683.7273. Page shows two hour statements: phone 'Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.' and office 'Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.'.
records.raw_hours_text: Our hours of operation are Monday through Friday from 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. | You can contact VWAP or VSTOP by calling (703) 746-4100 during office hours, Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Walk-in assistance is also available if you have a scheduled court appearance.

services.description: VSTOP domestic violence/sexual assault advocacy and Domestic Violence Intervention Specialist for survivors involved in the criminal justice process.
Victim-Witness Assistance: court accompaniment, rights information, victim impact statements, restitution and Criminal Injuries Compensation Fund claims (English and Spanish).

eligibility.details: Victims and witnesses of crime (criminal justice process in Alexandria).

records.organization_name: The Clothesline for Arlington Kids
records.location_name: The Clothesline for Arlington Kids
records.notes: Free clothing for school-aged children (K-12) from low-income families. Visits by appointment; online order with pickup also available. records.raw_eligibility_text: The Clothesline serves qualifying children attending school in Arlington (kindergarten to 12th grade). At this time, we do not serve pre-school students. Present a referral letter from a school social worker, a local social services organization, or a place of worship. If your child attends a community eligibility school you may present a screenshot of their current class schedule in ParentVue.

services.description: Qualifying students select a full wardrobe of clothing twice a year, free of charge.

eligibility.details: Students and their families must make an appointment at The Clothesline in advance.

records.organization_name: Culmore Clinic
records.location_name: Culmore Clinic
records.notes: Nonprofit, heavily volunteer-run clinic offering free medical care, counseling (licensed volunteer mental health professionals), and specialty referrals to uninsured adults in the Bailey's Crossroads/Falls Church area. Also HIV and STD testing, physical therapy, EKGs and dental services (https://www.culmoreclinic.org/care). New patients register by calling 703-260-8429 (enrollment page); appointment line on contact page is 703-260-8413. 8-10 week wait list for new patients. Sources conflict on days (three vs four days a week) and on the 200% FPL example amounts ($2,600/month vs $2,265/month for an individual). Follows Fairfax County Schools for weather/holiday closures. Mailing: PO Box 8332, Falls Church, VA 22041. Hours from https://www.culmoreclinic.org/contact.

records.raw_eligibility_text: Clinic patients’ income must be at 200% of Federal Poverty Level or below (e.g. $2,600/month or $31,200/year for an individual and $4,625/month or $55,500/year for a family of 4). ... All patients are required to bring the following to their registration appointment: Proof of income (pay stub, W2 form, or a letter from an employer stating rate of pay) Proof of Fairfax County residence
